nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Strong equatorial sun powers the seagrass, algae and corals of the shallow lagoon and the rainforest on the islands.

nodes.name: Warm, clear lagoon water
nodes.desc: Shallow, sheltered water inside the barrier reefs lets light reach seagrass beds and reef flats. Heat waves and silt are threats to such water.

nodes.name: Heavy rainfall
nodes.desc: Frequent rain feeds the island forest and sends fresh water and sediment down to mangroves and the lagoon.

nodes.name: Nutrients
nodes.desc: Nutrients from forest litter, mangrove mud and recycled dead matter support plant growth on land and in the shallows.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Bacteria, fungi and small invertebrates break down dead plants and animals and return nutrients to the mud and water.

nodes.name: Mangrove
nodes.desc: A mangrove tree of tidal shores in the western Pacific, recorded near the lagoon. Mangrove stands shelter the shoreline and young animals.

nodes.name: Seagrass
nodes.desc: Small seagrasses of shallow sandy lagoon floors. Dugongs and green turtles graze seagrass meadows.

nodes.name: Reef algae
nodes.desc: Calcified green algae and other algae growing on reef flats and rock. They feed parrotfish, surgeonfish and green turtles.

nodes.name: Fig trees
nodes.desc: Rainforest figs bear fruit that is eaten by fruit bats and fruit pigeons. Weeping fig was among the plants recorded near the lagoon.

nodes.name: Island imperial pigeon
nodes.desc: A large fruit pigeon of Pacific island forests and coasts that feeds on fruit such as figs.

nodes.name: New Georgia monkey-faced bat
nodes.desc: A large fruit bat found in the Solomon Islands. Fruit bats eat fruit and are food for the Sanford's sea eagle.

nodes.name: Surgeonfish
nodes.desc: Reef fish that graze algae off rock and coral. Blacktip reef sharks and many fish-eating birds eat such reef fish.

nodes.name: Parrotfish
nodes.desc: Reef fish that scrape algae from rock with strong beaks. Their grazing keeps algae from smothering reef structure and makes sand.

nodes.name: Green sea turtle
nodes.desc: Adults graze seagrass and algae in shallow lagoons. Tiger sharks are their main predator.

nodes.name: Dugong
nodes.desc: A marine mammal that eats mainly seagrass, often whole plants. Its grazing and digging reshape seagrass beds.

nodes.name: Pacific reef heron
nodes.desc: A shoreline wader of reefs and rocky coasts, frequently recorded near the lagoon. It hunts small fish and crustaceans in shallows.

nodes.name: Osprey
nodes.desc: A fish-eating raptor that dives for prey in shallow water. Recorded around the lagoon.

nodes.name: Brahminy kite
nodes.desc: A coastal raptor that takes fish and other small prey and also feeds on dead animals along the shore.

nodes.name: Sanford's sea eagle
nodes.desc: Found only in the Solomon Islands. It eats mostly carrion along the tideline plus fish, and sometimes birds and fruit bats from the canopy.

nodes.name: Blacktip reef shark
nodes.desc: A shark of shallow reefs and sand flats that eats small reef fish such as surgeonfish. Tiger sharks sometimes prey on it.

nodes.name: Saltwater crocodile
nodes.desc: An ambush apex predator of mangroves, estuaries and coasts. Its range includes the Solomon Islands, and it takes fish, birds, crabs and sharks.

nodes.name: Tiger shark
nodes.desc: An open-water predator that hunts turtles of all sizes and also eats other sharks. The main natural predator of green turtles.
